title: Sensitive telemetry protection: selective redaction, role-scoped access, and retention harmonization
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Scope: Define and implement a coherent data-governance layer for telemetry (traces, metrics, logs) that achieves three goals: 1) deterministic PII-sensitive-field redaction at ingestion and on-demand rehydration controls; 2) role-scoped access and immutable access logging for auditability; 3) retention policy harmonization across stores (hot traces, long-term metrics, archived logs) with automated lifecycle enforcement.

Motivation: Customers and internal compliance require that telemetry not leak PII and that only authorized roles can retrieve sensitive traces. Current observability pipelines accept varied span/attribute names from instrumented services, which increases surface area for accidental sensitive data capture. Retention currently differs by store and is configured ad-hoc, leading to over-retention in some cases.

Out of scope: rewriting collectors, major schema changes to existing telemetry, or addressing proprietary ingestion from third-party agents (those will be handled via adapters).

Goals: 
- Build an ingestion layer plugin that performs configurable attribute-level redaction and tagging for traces/logs, with a small default rule-set to catch common PII patterns (emails, SSNs, credit-card-like numbers).
- Provide an RBAC enforcement layer integrated with the Console so role-scoped queries to traces/logs/metrics are enforced and all exports are recorded in access logs.
- Implement centralized retention policies expressed as a single source-of-truth policy manifest, translated to retention enforcement for each backend (clickhouse/elasticsearch/long-term-blob) with scheduled enforcement and alerting for drift.

Acceptance criteria: 
- New ingestion plugin is deployed to staging and drops or masks >95% of seeded PII test cases (see test matrix in linked doc).
- Console query endpoint rejects attempts to fetch redacted fields for roles without the "telemetry_sensitive_view" permission and returns an event id for audit.
- Access logs record: requestor identity, target resource (trace id/log id/metric series), query parameters, time, and whether redaction was applied. Logs stored for 1 year in audit index.
- Retention manifest applied to staging enforces target TTLs across stores and a nightly job reports any drift to #observability-alerts channel.

Non-functional constraints: 
- Redaction must add <3ms median overhead to ingestion pipeline for typical trace sizes.
- RBAC checks must be cached for 30s to avoid high QPS bottlenecks while still allowing quick policy revocation.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design: finalize policy schema (attribute rules, regex patterns, allowlist/denylist, transform types) and RBAC permission names (week 1).
2) Ingestion plugin: implement in collector layer (go) with pluggable rule engine and metrics exposing redaction counts by type (week 2-3).
3) Access control middleware: extend Console backend to call policy service for role-scoped filtration, and implement access logging (week 3-4).
4) Retention pipeline: author translator that applies manifest to each backend's retention mechanism and implement nightly drift scanner (week 4-5).
5) Testing & rollout: run privacy fuzz tests, load tests, and gradual rollout (canary -> 50% -> global) with rollback runbook (week 6).

Risk & mitigations: 
- False positives in regex redaction: mitigate by conservative default rules + customer opt-in stricter profiles and a training set for ML-assisted classification in a follow-up.
- Performance regression: add telemetry-specific metrics and safety throttle, allow bypass for high-throughput internal tenants.
- RBAC complexity for multi-team orgs: provide mapping utilities and default templates for common roles.

Operational playbook: 
- Dashboard: new "Telemetry Governance" console page with counts of redactions by type, retention compliance status, and access log error rates.
- Alerts: high redaction rate spiking (could indicate instrumentation regression) and retention drift >5% for any backend.
- Rollback: endpoint feature flag to disable ingestion redaction per-tenant; clear steps in runbook to revert policy manifest to previous version.

Stakeholders & reviewers: 
- Privacy & Legal: Marcus Li (review rules and retention windows)
- Security: Leila Karim (review access logging and audit retention)
- Platform SRE: Jordan Cole (validate performance and rollout strategy)

Dependencies & integrations: 
- Needs schema mapping work from SDK/agent teams to standardize common span attribute names (tracked separately).
- Relies on centralized identity service for requestor identity tokens.

Related links: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Governance+Design (internal)
- Test matrix: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/telemetry-governance-fuzz (internal)
- Draft retention manifest (yaml): https://ghe.redwood.ai/platform/observability/retention-manifest/-/blob/main/manifest.yaml

Notes (progress updates):
- 2025-02-18: Kickoff with privacy and security; agreed on 1-year audit log retention for access logs.
- 2025-02-25: Prototype regex rule engine completed; initial benchmark shows +1.6ms median ingestion overhead (OK).
- 2025-03-01: RBAC permission names finalized; working on Console enforcement stub.
- 2025-03-04: Discovered a gap where some third-party agents send base64-embedded JSON in a single attribute — added a decision to detect and apply nested redaction heuristics (will be in scope for phase 2 if CPU cost too high).

Follow-ups / Phase 2 ideas: ML-assisted PII detection, tenant-specific privacy profiles, encrypted-at-rest sensitive field vaulting with ephemeral rehydrate tokens, and automated customer notifications for blocked exports.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion plugin masks or flags >95% of seeded PII cases in staging
Console denies sensitive-field access to roles without 'telemetry_sensitive_view' and emits audit events
Access logs include identity, resource, params, time, redaction flag and are queryable for 1 year
Retention manifest translated and applied to all observability backends in staging with nightly drift reports
technical_notes: Prototype is in Go for the collector module. Use a small decision-table engine rather than full RE2 compilation per attribute to bound CPU. Export a prometheus metric obs_redaction_count{type,rule,tenant} and timing histograms. Cache RBAC responses in memory with TTL and metrics for cache hit/miss. Access log write path must be append-only and use existing audit-index pipeline; ensure schema includes trace/log identifiers for cross-correlation.
rollout_plan: Canary on staging -> internal prod orgs -> 10% tenants -> 50% -> 100%. Each stage must pass privacy fuzz-suite and perf benchmarks. Use feature-flag gate: 'telemetry_governance_v1' per-tenant. Monitor obs:redaction_latency,p50 ingestion, and audit_log_write_errors. Minimum 48h soak at each stage.
